title: Maximum Non-Overlapping Movies
statement:
A cinema shows `n` movies. Movie `i` starts at time `start[i]` and ends at time `end[i]`. You can watch only one movie at a time, and you must watch a movie from its start to its end.

Two movies **overlap** if some moment lies strictly inside both of them. A movie that starts exactly when another one ends does **not** overlap with it, so you may watch them back to back.

Return the maximum number of movies you can watch so that no two of the chosen movies overlap.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start[i]` and `end[i]`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the maximum number of movies that can be watched without any overlap.

examples.explanation: Watch the movies (1,3), (3,6) and (6,9): each starts when the previous one ends. No set of four movies is pairwise non-overlapping.
Every pair of movies overlaps, so only one movie can be watched.
The three short back-to-back movies (1,2), (2,3), (3,4) fit; the long movie (1,4) would block all of them.

hints: Try a greedy rule: among the movies you could still watch, which one should you pick first so that you keep as much time as possible for the rest?
Sort the movies by end time. Picking the movie that finishes earliest never hurts: any optimal schedule can swap its first movie for it.
Scan the sorted list, keeping the end time of the last watched movie. Take a movie when its start is at least that end time.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    mv = sorted((int(data[2 + 2 * i]), int(data[1 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n))
    last = -1
    cnt = 0
    for e, s in mv:
        if s >= last:
            cnt += 1
            last = e
    print(cnt)

main()

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
mv = [(int(data[1 + 2 * i]), int(data[2 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n)]
best = 0
for mask in range(1 << n):
    chosen = sorted(mv[i] for i in range(n) if mask >> i & 1)
    ok = all(chosen[j][1] <= chosen[j + 1][0] for j in range(len(chosen) - 1))
    if ok:
        best = max(best, len(chosen))
print(best)
